judged_text: updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares against the falsy externalCalendarId it is falling back from, so it always returns undefined and the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback is gone. Rescheduling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API, the update fails, and the event stays at the old time on the host's calendar while the Cal.com booking shows the new time — a silent divergence for exactly the legacy bookings the old fallback was serving.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback was changed to:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

This compares `cal.externalId` against `externalCalendarId` exactly in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it will almost always return `undefined`. The previous behavior (pre-refactor) fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single destination calendar) and would have selected the host’s destination calendar when no `externalCalendarId` was present. With the new array type, the code does not fall back to the first destination calendar (unlike other updated places that use `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). This is a real, diff-verifiable logic error that can cause updates to target no calendar / the wrong calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing (legacy references).
